claims.statement: EU repair rules require accessible repair information and reasonable spare-parts prices for covered goods, while the planned European platform is intended to help consumers find repairers; the founder can obtain a commercial control point by contracting end-of-line inventory from smaller appliance importers, holding pooled stock at a 3PL, and selling a cross-brand parts-availability SLA to repair networks.

Since 31 July 2026 consumers can require manufacturers to repair covered technically repairable goods within a reasonable time and price, and choosing repair extends the legal guarantee by at least 12 months; each unavailable long-tail part can therefore be measured as a missed repair, replacement or refund cost, service delay, and potential non-compliance event.

Manufacturers must provide covered repairs and reasonable access to spare parts, and the Commission expects the rules to generate 4.8 billion euros of EU growth and investment; appliance importers, manufacturers, warranty administrators, retailers, and repair franchises are identifiable payers using existing parts-inventory, warranty, service-level, and replacement budgets when a model approaches end of sale or a repair request arrives.

contrary_evidence: The repair obligation covers only product categories already subject to EU reparability requirements, not every appliance, and many original manufacturers already maintain sophisticated parts logistics.
Manufacturers may satisfy obligations through their own centralized inventory, and a January 2028 European repair platform may reduce the value of a standalone discovery channel.

economics.acquisition_route: Target three smaller Polish appliance or electronics importers with discontinued models; take consignment or call options on their end-of-line parts, place them at an existing 3PL, and sell a ninety-day fill-rate guarantee to two independent repair chains.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A pooled catalogue of 100000 low-volume parts producing an assumed 25 PLN monthly availability fee per active SKU plus parts margin and repair-network SLA fees could become a regional infrastructure layer; the valuable asset is demand and interchangeability data, not a one-off warehouse business.
economics.founder_time: Approximately 15-20 founder hours per week for demand forecasting, contracts, and exception pricing; warehouse fulfillment and technical inspection are outsourced.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Preliminary 35-55% blended gross margin from availability fees and 25-40% part markups after storage, pick-pack, returns, and obsolescence; initial inventory write-downs could make margin negative.
economics.payback: An importer should pay when annual SLA and pool fees are below the expected cost of emergency sourcing, whole-unit replacement, and holding every tail SKU itself; this requires model-level failure and stockout data.
economics.pricing: Assumed 10-40 PLN per active SKU per month for reserved availability, 25-40% transaction markup, and 100-500 PLN emergency fulfillment surcharge.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Repair networks order across recurring failures, while importers renew availability coverage for several years after each model stops selling; each new model cohort adds a new tail.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A cross-brand graph of model-to-part compatibility, failure timing, stockout frequency, repair conversion, and residual inventory value.
fingerprint.customer: Smaller EU appliance and electronics importers, warranty administrators, retailers, and independent repair networks lacking economical long-tail inventory.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Repair franchises, warranty administrators, parts distributors, and the future European repair discovery layer surface real demand; importers contribute end-of-line inventory under consignment or options.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A pooled long-tail spare-parts reserve with a contractually defined fill-rate and response-time SLA; revenue combines per-SKU availability, transaction margin, and emergency fulfillment.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: An importer, warranty administrator, or repair network pays from parts, warranty, or replacement budget when a model leaves active distribution or a covered repair request needs a scarce part.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A low-frequency component for a repairable product is no longer economical for one manufacturer to stock but is needed to meet a time-bounded repair obligation.

founder_fit: Demand forecasting and compatibility inference use the founder's data-science strengths.
The business can start with consigned inventory and outsourced fulfillment, keeping capital and daily labor bounded.
Sales can be concentrated through a few importers and repair chains rather than constant consumer-facing interaction.
risks: Obsolescence, counterfeit parts, safety defects, and product-liability exposure could erase the inventory margin.
Technical IP or tooling may prevent third-party fabrication and leave the pool dependent on OEM supply.
Incumbent parts distributors may bundle an SLA once demand becomes visible.

structure.control_point: Consignment or call options over end-of-line spare parts combined with a repair-network fill-rate SLA.
structure.critical_dependency: Cross-customer demand aggregation must lower inventory cost enough to cover obsolescence and safety liability.

thesis: Right-to-repair makes a low-frequency spare part economically important after ordinary distribution has moved on. By pooling end-of-line inventory and demand across smaller brands, a neutral operator can sell availability rather than software, earn on each repair, and learn which parts are interchangeable and when they fail, creating a cross-brand asset OEM silos do not share.
title: Long-Tail Spare-Parts Availability Pool
uncertainties: Which covered product categories show the highest whole-unit replacement cost caused specifically by unavailable parts?
Will importers consign inventory or demand that the pool purchase it outright?
What fill-rate and retention period will national enforcement treat as a reasonable repair timeframe?
